questions.question: Why does React need keys when rendering lists?
questions.title: React Lists Keys
questions.direct_answer: Keys give each item in a list a stable identity so React's diff can match old and new items across renders. Without keys (or with index keys), reorders and insertions shift positions and React destroys/recreates nodes or reuses the wrong ones — causing lost state and stale renders. Keys must be unique among siblings, stable across renders, and derived from data (an id), not the array index.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph without-keys
        A1[old: A B C] --> P[positional match]
        B1[new: Z A B C] --> P
        P --> X[all nodes rebuilt]
    end
    subgraph with-keys
        A2[old: keys a b c] --> K[key match]
        B2[new: keys z a b c] --> K
        K --> Y[a b c preserved, z created]
    end
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
What the diff actually does (the mechanism): React's reconciliation matches children of the same parent. When children are keyed, the diff builds a map of old-children-by-key and walks the new list — a key present in both is moved/reused (preserving its DOM node AND its state), a new key is created, a missing key is unmounted. Without keys, the fallback is positional: child at slot i matches child at slot i, and different type or content destroys the subtree.

The state-preservation detail (the depth marker): preserving the node preserves hook state — a keyed row that moves keeps its useState values, its input focus, its scroll position. This is why the unkeyed-to-do-list bug is so visible: component instances survive position changes when keyed, and their state follows the INSTANCE, not the data.

The random-key anti-pattern (worth naming): `key={Math.random()}` regenerates every render → every item is a 'new' item → full teardown every render. Same for `key={JSON.stringify(item)}` — it's unstable if the item mutates. The key should come from the data's identity field; when data has no id (static config lists), index is acceptable because the list never changes shape.
